title: Annotatio III §.IX: ENIM partly aetiological, partly promissive — baptism parallel (Mark 16:16)
pass_a_gloss: As partly aetiological, giving the reason why that which was being offered was to be eaten and drunk, partly promissive, because the promise proper to every Sacrament is read expressed in Baptism in these express words: Whoever shall have believed and been baptized shall be saved.
pass_b_english: ENIM is partly aetiological — why what was offered was to be eaten and drunk.
Partly promissive — like Baptism’s own promise: whoever believes and is baptized shall be saved.
source_text: Ceu ætiologica partim, rationem reddente, quare illud, quòd porrigebatur, edendum bibendumque fuerit, partim promissiva, quòd promissio omni Sacramento propria, in Baptismate disertis his verbis expressa legatur: Quicunque crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, salvabitur.
